identity_notes: The catalogue's BMH footprint (bmh + bmh-31068-0) is several buildings of different dates fused together, and they read very differently: (1) the ORIGINAL B.C. Matthews Hall (late 1960s/70s): darker brown-red brick, long continuous ribbon windows with dark-bronze frames, ground floors set back behind square brick piers with a sloping dark-metal skirt (W23-W27 east block, 3 storeys, 11.5 m), and the 2-storey middle block (W10-W12, W21, 7.5 m) with punched upper windows and bronze-panel-framed ground windows; (2) the 2003 Teeple 'Lyle S. Hallman Institute' work in lighter orange-red brick with grey-aluminium curtain walls: the north wing W1-W9 (3-storey curtain wall between brick towers, the main LHI entrance canopy at W0/W31 with the 'LYLE S. HALLMAN INSTITUTE FOR HEALTH PROMOTION' panel, sv_W0, sv_W1, 2025), and the south block W14-W17 (see next note); (3) a 1-storey orange-brick wing W18-W20 with a timber slat fence and white soffit, and the beige-panel 'APPLIED HEALTH SCIENCES' entrance on W22.

LHI's spec says a brick block east of the LHI N-S passage carries the LHI name sign but is catalogued as BMH. CONFIRMED. sv_W15_-Lcfn (Sep 2014, camera at about (746,443) looking 339 deg) shows it square-on: the passage runs NNW between LHI (cantilevered brick, left) and this block (right), under a glazed level-2 bridge; the block's SE face is BMH W15, and the bronze letters 'LYLE S. HALLMAN / INSTITUTE / FOR HEALTH PROMOTION' sit on its level-2 brick at about s 8-11.5. The 'N-S passage' is the slit along BMH W14 / LHI W11 (W14 runs at 330 deg), which is why the lidar shows 0-1 m there. The brick (orange-red, light mortar) and the details (aluminium ribbon glazing, beige-soffit glazed corner box on a thin steel post) match Teeple's LHI, not the old BMH. Google Earth labels a pin 'Lyle Hallman North' over the southern part of this footprint (bmh_study.jpg, lower-left orbit view). So W14-W17 (and probably the W18-W20 low wing) are really part of LHI that the City outline merged into BMH. The model can keep them in BMH's mesh but should colour and detail them like LHI (brick_orange); a second, wall-mounted copy of the same sign is on BMH W0 at the north (Ring Road) entrance, and a free-standing monument sign 'B. C. MATTHEWS HALL / LYLE S. HALLMAN INSTITUTE FOR HEALTH PROMOTION' stands on the lawn in front of W20.

geometry_notes: North wing courtyard face W4-W8 is drawn about 2.5-3 m too far north: lidar profiles across W5 and W7 stay at 12 m for 2.5-3 m outside the line, then drop to 0. W23 is about 1.5-2 m too far north as well (the real face is further S).
W14 s 0-5 is not building (nDSM 1.0-1.3 m): the footprint's NW end of W14 overlaps the open walkway/passage between LHI W11 and this block.

W13 (6.6 m) sits under a 5 m roof plane (lidar 5 m everywhere around it): it is the low roof/portico zone by the LHI entrance plaza; LHI's spec owns the portico. Treat W13 as a recessed glazed stair wall under that roof.

W0 and W31 (3.5-3.9 m) are the outline of the north entrance canopy, not walls: a thin flat canopy on the brick vestibule, one brick pier at its west end (sv_W0, sv_W1). Draw a canopy slab about 3.3 m up with a 0.35 m dark fascia, not a 3.7 m box.

W20 is a 3.5 m one-storey wing about 5 m deep; behind it a 7.5 m wall (not in walls.json) carries a row of about 14 small square clerestory windows (about 0.7 x 0.6 m at z 5.4-6.0, pitch about 1.4 m) under a brick parapet (sv_W20_1AJ, earth_W18/W20). The same 7.5 m wall shows behind W18.
The east block (W23-W27) roof is 11.4 m but W25 (service/stair tower) is 13.6 m; W1 (LHI entrance tower) is 13.0 m with a lower front mass at about 11.8 m (two stepped brick masses, sv_W1).
Ground is nearly flat around the north and east; it falls about 1.5-2 m toward the south (W15-W20 lawns slope down to the SE, low brick retaining wall and steps at W15 s 15-19).
